Austrian media suggest the dismissal may stem from domestic political competition ahead of potential e

Speaking at a defense summit, Ratcliffe noted these cost-effective systems help Ukraine counter Russia’s manpower advantage, as US officials estimate Russian losses at 7,000 soldiers weekly.

Fedorov is emerging as a challenger to Zelensky | Bohdan Nahaylo — The dismissal of Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered public protests and exposed a divide between his technology-focused approach and the traditional methods of Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrsky. Kyiv Post Editor-in-Chief noted that President Volodymyr Zelensky’s decision to side with Syrsky has politically galvanized younger Ukrainians who view Fedorov as a reformer.

Schrödinger’s Elections — Russians are slated to go to the polls from Sept. 18 to 20, during which 450 seats of the Russian Federation’s State Duma will be decided. Whether or not real elections will take place has become an ontological problem akin to the Schrödinger cat paradox of quantum mechanics.

She succeeds Julie Davis, who concluded her diplomatic mission as the acting head of the embassy in Ukraine on June 27.

The targeted ships included dry cargo vessels, tankers, and floating cranes. This latest strike brings the total number of vessels hit during the 13-day Operation “Molochka” to 172.

Germany and France Sign Agreement on Defense Cooperation and Nuclear Deterrence — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron signed an agreement to integrate conventional military capabilities and missile defense with nuclear deterrence. Following the halt of their joint fighter jet and tank programs, the countrie

Fires broke out at a Noginsk oil depot in the Moscow region and two major Wildberries logistics complexes in Kotovsk (Tambov region) and Elektrostal (Moscow region). Local authorities in the Tambov region reported the deaths of seven Wildberries employees.

Russian Strikes Target Odesa Port, UN Warehouse in Dnipro, Bus in Marhanets — On Friday, July 17, Russian forces conducted multiple strikes across Ukraine, targeting port infrastructure in the Odesa region, a UN World Food Programme warehouse in Dnipro, and a civilian bus in Marhanets. Russia Strikes Kharkiv, Chernihiv Region, Kills 1, Wounds 21 — Russian armed forces killed one civilian and injured at least 21 others across the Kharkiv and Chernihiv regions on Friday, including eight children. The attacks targeted residential areas in Izium, Kharkiv city, and Novhorod-Siverskyi, damaging civilian infrastructure.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, July 17, 2026 — Latest from the Institute for the Study of War.

Lavrov’s New Deal: Why Azerbaijan Is Locking In a 2-Year Plan With Moscow After Backing Ukraine — Azerbaijan is deepening diplomatic and transportation cooperation with Russia even as Ilham Aliyev publicly backs Ukraine, revealing a strategy aimed at preserving ties with Moscow while maintaining geopolitical room to maneuver.

Tusk Welcomes Zelensky’s 5-Point Plan as Poland-Ukraine Tensions Ease — Poland and Ukraine signaled readiness to ease bilateral tensions as Tusk backed Zelensky’s five-point plan focused on diplomacy, archives, exhumations, societal dialogue and historical memory.

Ukraine Marks 12 Years Since MH17 Downing, An Act of Russian Terror — President Volodymyr Zelensky marked the 12th anniversary of the MH17 downing – an act of Russian terror – and urged the world not to turn a blind eye to Russia’s crimes.

Drones Strike Russian-Occupied Crimea, Fire Reported Near Gvardeyskoye Airfield — Russian-occupied Crimea came under an overnight drone attack, with a fire reported near the Gvardeyskoye military airfield and possible strikes around Sevastopol’s Balaklava Thermal Power Plant, according to Krymsky Veter.

Kyiv Placed on Alert Twice Overnight Over Ballistic Missile Threat — Ukraine’s Air Force issued two ballistic missile warnings overnight, prompting Kyiv authorities to urge residents to seek shelter. The second alert was lifted at 2:06 a.m., with no strikes, damage or casualties reported.

Russia Prepares Black Sea Fleet Family Evacuation From Crimea – Leaked Order — Leaked documents published by Void Group indicate that Russian military authorities are collecting information on Black Sea Fleet families who could be evacuated from occupied Crimea. The reported order comes amid intensified Ukrainian strikes.

Former Navalny Accuser Arrested After Turning Against Putin — Russian activist Ilya Remeslo, who previously helped prosecute Kremlin critic Alexei Navalny, has been detained on charges of spreading “fake information” about the military. His arrest follows a dramatic break with the Kremlin, during which he called for Vladimir Putin to stand trial and predicted the Russian leader would be removed in handcuffs.

Russia Continues to Produce Missiles Using Foreign Parts — Authorities say Russia continues building missiles using foreign parts from countries such as Switzerland, China and the US, alongside Russian and Belarusian components, based on the forensic analysis of debris from a Russian strike on Bila Tserkva in May.

Ukraine Pledges to Grant Poland Access on Volhynia Files — President Volodymyr Zelensky announced a five-point plan to strengthen ties with Poland following a recent diplomatic rift. Ukraine agreed to grant additional permits for exhumation of the historical sites, while boosting joint capabilities to advance bilateral ties.

Sybiha Appointed as Acting FM, Khmara as MD Amid Cabinet Reshuffle — New Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi appointed acting ministers of defense and foreign affairs, while announcing a restructuring of several government bodies. He also set a deadline for ministries to submit priority action plans by Aug. 5.

Putin Just GUTTED Russia to Keep His War Alive — At that pace, capturing the remaining Ukrainian-held territory in Donetsk would take another 14 years and millions more Russian casualties explains Kyiv Post Special Correspondent Jason Jay Smart.

Kremlin Denies Interference in Trump’s Election — Kremlin firmly rejected US intelligence claims of Russia’s election interference made by President Trump during his speech at the White House. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov called the allegations of Russia being a threat to America’s voting system unsubstantiated, while China separately denied similar claims.

Russian Orthodox Church Structures Pose as Ukrainian Communities to Influence Refugees — A study by the Institute of National Stability and Security alleges that Russian Orthodox Church structures in Europe are disguising themselves as Ukrainian religious communities to influence Ukrainian refugees. Researchers say the network operates through hundreds of parishes, social initiatives, and Telegram channels that promote pro-Russian narratives.

Naftogaz Names Fedorenko Acting CEO After Koretskyi Becomes Prime Minister — Serhiy Fedorenko, a Naftogaz Group board member with over a decade in the oil and gas industry and a stint as a volunteer in Ukraine's Armed Forces, will lead the company on an acting basis. His immediate mandate: keeping heating-season preparations on pace, securing gas reserves in storage, and repairing infrastructure battered by systematic Russian strikes.

Day Two of Fedorov Protests Sees Hundreds Rally Across Ukraine — Protests supporting Fedorov expanded to several Ukrainian cities. Demonstrators demanded his reinstatement, criticized the lack of explanation for his dismissal, and called on the Verkhovna Rada to return from recess and appoint a new defense minister promptly.

Russia Avoids Mentioning Mobilization Before Autumn’s Elections, Ukraine Says — An officer from Ukraine’s Military Intelligence (HUR) said Russia has avoided talking about mobilization ahead of autumn’s elections, though the risks remain. He added that Russia has existing infrastructure for mobilization – it just needs more “cannon fodder” to fill the training grounds.

Zelensky Offers Former Interior Minister Klymenko National Security and Defense Council Job — Zelensky offered former interior minister Klymenko the position of secretary of Ukraine’s National Security and Defense Council (RNBO) on Friday. Klymenko was originally handpicked to become the new defense minister, but popular protests over the removal of former Defense Minister Fedorov have complicated Zelensky’s plans.

Trump Accuses China of Interfering in 2020 Election During Prime-Time Address — President Donald Trump accused China of interfering in the 2020 US election during a televised address from the White House, although his claims remain unverified. Critics argued the speech was aimed at casting doubt on the electoral process ahead of the upcoming congressional midterm elections.

Zelensky Offers Taras Kachka Post as Ukraine’s EU Representative — President Volodymyr Zelensky has offered former Deputy Prime Minister for European and Euro-Atlantic Integration Taras Kachka to head Ukraine’s representation to the EU in Brussels. The role would include supporting Ukraine’s accession talks and serving as the country’s trade representative in relations with key partners.

Russia Hails Drop in Beer Imports From ‘Unfriendly Countries’ — Russia said beer imports from “unfriendly countries” fell 36% year on year, while beer consumption rose slightly to 3.1 billion liters in the first half of 2026, state media RIA Novosti reported. The research center behind the data noted, however, that the figures cover all countries outside the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), not just those Russia classifies as “unfriendly.”

Ukraine Knocks Out Tu-95 Bomber Used to Rain Missiles on Ukrainian Cities — Ukraine’s SBU said it destroyed a Tu-95 strategic bomber at Russia’s Engels air base after an 800-km (500-mile) drone strike. Zelensky said the aircraft had been used in missile attacks on Ukraine and called the operation another successful “long-range sanction.”

Putin's Approval Rating Sees Biggest Weekly Drop Since 2022 Amid Fuel Crisis — State-linked polls recorded Putin's sharpest weekly approval decline since 2022, with support falling 5 percentage points. Fedorov Ouster Exposes Power Struggle Around Zelensky — Fedorov’s public confrontation with Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrsky, support from military figures and protests across Ukraine have turned a government reshuffle into a serious test of President Volodymyr Zelensky’s authority.

Ukrainian Intel Warns of Russian Campaign to Target Frontline Civilian Logistics — Ukraine’s Military Intelligence (HUR) said Russia’s Rubikon drone unit had been ordered to target civilian gas stations, trucks, buses, and cars in frontline regions in a new campaign, urging residents to remain vigilant, while accusing Russian special services of staging false-flag attacks by striking their own civilians.

Hungary's Former PM Szijjártó to Work for Chinese Carmaker BYD — Former Hungarian Foreign Minister Peter Szijjártó said Wednesday that he resigned from parliament to work for Chinese carmaker BYD as "head of the group's external relations," with the country having negotiated a deal to build a factory in Hungary under his government to dodge EU tariffs.

Anti-Ukrainian Hate Incidents Surge in Poland Amid Online Hostility — Reports of anti-Ukrainian incidents in Poland are increasing, with experts linking the trend to election politics, historical disputes, and Russian disinformation campaigns that seek to undermine relations between the two neighboring countries.

Putin Leading Russia to ‘Chaos’, Anti-War Politician Says — Russian anti-war politician says Putin is steering the country toward chaos as authorities seek to block his election bid through arrest, extremism charges, and a travel ban, underscoring the Kremlin’s widening crackdown on dissent ahead of September’s parliamentary vote.

Ukraine Says It Hit 159 Russian Shadow Fleet Vessels in 12 Days — USF say they struck 159 Russian shadow fleet vessels in 12 days, including 12 ships hit on July 17, aiming to disrupt oil and cargo shipments used to bypass sanctions while avoiding oil spills by disabling rather than sinking the ships.

Busification: Is the Ukraine Army Crisis Real? | Eastern Express — Kyiv Post’s Stefan Korshak explains how Ukraine’s controversial mobilization system is fueling public frustration, why reform is urgently needed, and how the country can strengthen its army without weakening the social cohesion vital to resisting Russia.

Ukraine Strikes Kerch Rail Hub, Russian Vessels as Moscow Rushes to Protect Tankers — Ukraine reportedly struck a key railway hub in occupied Kerch and targeted six Russian tankers overnight. Ukrainian sources say the attacks are forcing Moscow to militarize its “shadow fleet” by deploying troops and air-defense teams aboard commercial vessels.

2 Killed, 8 Wounded in Russian Missile Strike on Odesa — A Russian missile strike on Odesa late Thursday killed two people and wounded eight others, including two children, while damaging several civilian sites.

Ukraine Disables 11 Russian ‘Shadow Fleet’ Vessels in Black Sea and Sea of Azov in a Single Day — Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces disabled 11 Russian shadow fleet vessels on Thursday, bringing the total targeted during Operation “MoLoChKa” to 147.

Ukraine Repatriates 501 Bodies Claimed to Be Fallen Soldiers — Ukraine repatriated 501 bodies that Russia claims belong to Ukrainian military personnel. Identification efforts are underway, coordinated by a wide network of state agencies and the Red Cross.

Zelensky Honors Turkish FM Fidan With Order of Merit — President Zelensky met with Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan and awarded him the Order of Merit, 2nd degree. The two discussed diplomacy, bilateral relations and trade cooperation between Ukraine and Turkey.

Zelensky Says New PM's Energy Expertise Vital for Ukraine's Winter Survival — President Volodymyr Zelensky praised new Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi’s record leading Naftogaz and Ukrnafta as Ukraine’s new government began work. Zelensky said winter preparedness and faster follow-through with international partners remain top priorities.

‘No One Is in Charge’: Fedorov Says Sumy Region Has No Clear Air Defense Command — Mykhailo Fedorov, former defense minister, called for accountability in frontline air defense and urged new jets to target those responsible for the strikes on Sumy region. Despite multiple troop groupings operating there, no single official commands air defense over the region, he said.

Kyiv: From Kyivan Rus to Hidden Courtyards — On Sunday, July 19, Language Lab is running a three-hour walking tour marking the Baptism of Kyivan Rus Day, tracing Prince Volodymyr’s unlikely rise and his decision to Christianize Kyiv. The English-language walk covers hidden courtyards, a former Soviet anti-religious museum, Igor Sikorsky’s home, and more.

Russia Strikes Zaporizhzhia, Kills 3, Injures 2, Including a Child — Russian armed forces struck Zaporizhzhia on Thursday, killing three people and injuring two others, including a child. A residential house caught fire and nearby buildings sustained blast damage.

Zelensky Names SBU’s Khmara Acting Defense Minister, Cites Strike Operations Experience — President Zelensky appointed Yevhen Khmara, who is currently serving as the Acting Head of the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU), to the position of acting defense minister, citing his experience leading long-range strike operations and Ukraine’s Alpha special forces unit. Zelensky plans to seek parliamentary approval for the permanent post soon. Some have questioned the legality of the move.

Montenegro Sets Oct. 1 Deadline to End Visa-Free Travel for Russians — Montenegro plans to end visa-free entry for Russian citizens starting Oct. 1, according to local outlet Dan. The change is part of broader EU-aligned migration reform that could also affect five other countries.

No Defense Minister, Protests in the Streets – Ukraine Edges Toward Political Crisis — President Volodymyr Zelensky proposed a new government without appointing a defense minister after the planned dismissal of reformist Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. The 16-member cabinet includes a mix of returning ministers and new appointments, while the positions of defense minister and foreign minister remain vacant pending presidential nominations.

Melnichenko omits Russia's war crimes and unprovoked aggression in Ukraine. Who Is Mykhailo Fedorov? — An illuminating early interview given by Mykhailo Fedorov to Kyiv Post’s Chief Editor Bohdan Nahayloin June 2022 about his vision and approach to developing Ukraine’s defense potential.

UK to Provide £300M for Ukraine in Joint Initiative With Sweden — On Thursday, the UK will allocate £300 million to work with Sweden on supplying Ukraine with 15 modern aircraft intended to strengthen Ukraine’s air defenses. The announcement came during British Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s visit to Kyiv, where he also called for increased pressure on Russia.

Fedorov: Open Tenders Saved Ukraine $100M, Threatened Powerful Interests — Fedorov said procurement reforms replaced direct contracts with competitive tenders, saving more than $100 million on artillery alone. He also alleged entrenched corruption within the Defense Ministry and said several officials linked to private interests were dismissed.

Top Cabinet Posts Vacant After Defense Minister-Army Chief Clash — Zelensky’s plan for a government reshuffle, with the appointment of new prime minister Serhiy Koretskyi on Thursday, has been upset by the surprise dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov.

Zelensky Says Fedorov-Syrsky Dispute ‘Problem of the Parties, but Also Mine’ — On Thursday, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukrainians were right to protest following the dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, saying that freedom of expression remains a core democratic value.

Sweden Commits $145M to New World Bank Facility Supporting Ukraine — On Wednesday, the Swedish government approved a $145 million contribution to the World Bank’s new IDA Crisis Facility 2.0 for Ukraine. Crimea's Dzhankoy Throttles Mobile Internet Amid Worsening Blackouts — Russian officials in occupied Crimea’s Dzhankoy have announced restrictions on mobile communication, with it available only between 8 a.m. and noon, then between 2 p.m. and 6 p.m. each day as the power crisis worsens following waves of Ukrainian attacks.

Fedorov Rejects Adviser Role, Says His Goal Was to ‘Win the War’ — Ukraine’s outgoing defense minister said he rejected Zelensky's offer to become an adviser after being removed from office. He argued that nationwide protests were driven by fears that military reforms could stall, not by support for him personally.

Russia’s Max Messenger Removed From Google Play — Russia’s Max messenger was no longer available on the Google Play Store on Thursday, two days after the EU imposed sanctions on its parent company. While it remains unclear whether the removal was linked to the sanctions, Apple took a similar step in June amid criticism that the app enables Kremlin surveillance.

Russia Asks India for More Gasoline as Refining Capacity Collapses — Russian oil giants have reportedly approached Indian refineries for more gasoline imports as the fuel crisis worsens. At least 40,000 metric tons are reportedly en route, but New Delhi and the refineries are denying involvement while sources told Reuters that the shipments are likely routed through traders via ship-to-ship transfers.

Zelensky’s Party May Delay Defense Minister Vote as Pro-Fedorov Protests Spread — Servant of the People lawmakers called an emergency party meeting amid signs that President Volodymyr Zelensky may lack sufficient support to replace Mykhailo Fedorov with Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko.

3 Poems by Vasyl Barka — On the 118th anniversary of his birth, Kyiv Post presents three of Vasyl Barka’s poems translated into English. Considered one of Ukraine’s most important 20th century writers, Barka’s deep vein of Christian mysticism and hope penetrates and illumines the horrors of a century he witnessed firsthand.

Fedorov Accuses Syrsky of ‘Thinking How to Split the Country, Not Defeat Russia’ — Fedorov has accused Ukraine’s commander-in-chief of blocking military reforms and refusing to acknowledge problems within the military. He called for changes in the military’s top leadership while defending his record on drones, robotics, and air defense.

Ukraine Should Send Washington a Soldier, Not Another Politician — By choosing a career diplomat for the post of ambassador to the US, Zelensky would only be playing into the hands of those who would turn Ukraine into a political football. What’s needed is someone who knows drones and would have the Pentagon’s ear.

SBU Sea Drones Hit 2 Shadow Fleet Tankers in Black Sea — The SBU said it struck two sanctioned Russian tankers – the Louise 1 and Banda – using its Mamai naval drones in cooperation with the Ukrainian Navy. It did not specify the date of the operation, but footage suggests the attacks took place off Russia’s Black Sea coast, some distance off the coastal cities of Novorossiysk and Sochi.

Rada Appoints Koretsky as Ukraine’s Prime Minister in Sweeping Wartime Cabinet Reshuffle — Ukraine’s parliament approved Koretsky as prime minister, completing a key step in Zelensky’s government reshuffle. While 289 lawmakers backed his appointment, questions remain over who will take over key ministerial positions in his cabinet – including the defense minister role.

UK Launches ‘Russia Inquiry,’ Describes Russia as Most ‘Acute’ Threat — The UK has launched a broad inquiry into Russia after its latest security reviews labelled Moscow the most “acute” threat to British interests. The new Inquiry will assess Russia’s alliances, foreign policy aims, and the conditions for any Ukraine settlement, alongside Russia’s internal governance, economic stability, and civil society. ‘No Good Options’: Why EU-Ukraine Defense Deal is Bad News for Putin — Security analyst Notte says Europe now views Ukraine as a strategic security asset, accelerating defense cooperation. She warns Moscow may respond with hybrid attacks and could test NATO’s resolve, although the alliance continues to serve as a powerful deterrent.

Senior Air Force Commander Quits, Calls Fedorov’s Dismissal ‘Great Evil’ — Ukraine's Air Force Deputy Commander resigned after Defense Minister Fedorov's dismissal, calling it "a great evil" for national defense. Yelizarov's resignation comes as parliament considers Zelensky's new Cabinet and defense leadership.

‘Change or Perish’: Thousands Rally in Kyiv Against Fedorov’s Dismissal — Thousands rallied in central Kyiv against Defense Minister Fedorov’s dismissal, arguing his removal threatens wartime reforms. The protest comes as lawmakers prepare to approve Ukraine’s new government.

Outgoing UK PM Starmer Visits Ukraine — Outgoing UK PM visits Kyiv for talks with Zelensky before leaving office next week. Starmer v is expected to reaffirm Britain’s long-term support for Ukraine and assure Kyiv that the change in leadership will not alter UK policy.

The Ankara NATO Summit: A Minor Respite for NATO — Since his re-election, Donald Trump has gravely damaged the NATO alliance by halting aid to Ukraine, appeasing Vladimir Putin, launching an unprovoked war on Iran, and undermining European allies. The Ankara summit’s final communiqué lays claims of unity and resolve which are largely false. Europe must maintain its own resolve – building its own independent defense since the US can no longer be trusted.

Why Ukrainians Are Outraged by Fedorov’s Dismissal — Zelensky’s government reshuffle has sparked widespread criticism in Ukraine, particularly with the dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who was widely viewed as the architect of the country’s military digitalization and the recent surge in drone capabilities. The decision has prompted calls for protests.
